target: थाने में चोरी की रिपोर्ट दर्ज कराई।
english: A theft report was filed at the police station.
tip: कराई (karaai) means having it done, not doing it yourself: रिपोर्ट दर्ज कराई = got the report registered, via the police. करना (karna) = do, कराना (karaana) = have done.

target: यह किताब साढ़े तीन सौ पन्नों की है।
english: This book has three hundred and fifty pages.
tip: साढ़े (saadhe) = 'plus a half': साढ़े तीन सौ (saadhe teen sau) = three and a half hundreds = 350 – not 'three hundred fifty'.

target: तेज़ बारिश में छाता बहुत काम आता है।
english: An umbrella is very useful in heavy rain.
tip: Useful things 'come to work': छाता बहुत काम आता है (kaam aata hai) = 'the umbrella comes to use'. काम आना is the everyday way to say something helps.

target: खिड़की से बाहर देखो, बारिश हो रही है।
english: Look outside from the window, it is raining.
tip: Rain is a thing that happens, not a verb: बारिश हो रही है (baarish ho rahi hai) = 'rain is happening'. There is no verb 'to rain' – बारिश is a noun and होना (hona) does the work.

target: बस स्टॉप हमारे घर के पास है।
english: The bus stop is near our house.
tip: के पास (ke paas) here is 'near': घर के पास = near the house. With a person it means having – मेरे पास किताब है (mere paas kitaab hai) = I have a book.

target: पैसे मेरे खाते में भेज देना।
english: Send the money to my account.
tip: The plain -ना form makes a gentle, do-it-later request: भेज देना (bhej dena) = 'send it (when you get to it)'. Softer and less immediate than भेजो (bhejo).

target: ऊँची इमारत से पूरा शहर दिखाई देता है।
english: The entire city is visible from the tall building.
tip: Visibility is given in Hindi: दिखाई देता है (dikhai deta hai) = 'gives being-seen'. The city is the giver and you receive the view.

target: दूध फ्रिज में रख दो।
english: Put the milk in the fridge.
tip: रख दो (rakh do) adds देना (dena = give) to the putting – the दो marks it as fully done, often for someone else's benefit. Plain रखो (rakho) is just 'put'.

target: शादी में छत्तीस तरह के पकवान बने थे।
english: Thirty-six types of dishes were made at the wedding.
tip: Every number up to 100 is its own word: छत्तीस (chhattis = 36) is not built from 'thirty' plus 'six'. All hundred get memorized one by one.

target: मैं तुमसे पाँच बजे स्टेशन पर मिलूँगा।
english: I'll meet you at the station at five.
tip: पाँच बजे (paanch baje) = 'five having rung' – clock time counts bell strikes. बजना (bajna) means to ring, so 'at five' is literally five chimes.

target: बस स्टॉप पर मेरा इंतज़ार करना।
english: Wait for me at the bus stop.
tip: You do someone's waiting: मेरा इंतज़ार करना (mera intezaar karna) = 'do my waiting'. The person waited for becomes a possessive, not 'for me'.

target: उसने बारिश में भीगते हुए स्कूल तक दौड़ लगाई।
english: She ran to school while getting wet in the rain.
tip: भीगते हुए (bheegte hue) = 'while getting soaked' – the -ते हुए ending runs one action in the background while the main one happens.

target: घर से बाज़ार तक पैदल दस मिनट लगते हैं।
english: It takes ten minutes to walk from home to the market.
tip: The minutes do the taking: दस मिनट लगते हैं (das minute lagte hain) = 'ten minutes attach'. With लगना (lagna), time is the subject – nobody takes it.

target: मेरी बेटी की सगाई अगले महीने होने वाली है।
english: My daughter's engagement is going to happen next month.
tip: होने वाली है (hone wali hai) = 'is about to happen'. वाला after a verb means on-the-verge – closer and more certain than plain future tense.

target: आज सड़क पर बहुत ट्रैफ़िक है।
english: There's a lot of traffic on the road today.
tip: There's no 'there is' – just है at the end: सड़क पर बहुत ट्रैफ़िक है (sadak par bahut traffic hai) = 'on the road much traffic is'.

target: पूजा ने बिना किसी की मदद के काम पूरा किया।
english: Pooja completed the work without anyone's help.
tip: बिना (bina = without) wraps its phrase from both ends: बिना किसी की मदद के (bina kisi ki madad ke) – बिना opens, के closes. Don't drop the closing के.

target: गौरव जी, कैसे हैं आप?
english: Gaurav ji, how are you?
tip: जी (ji) after a name adds warm respect: गौरव जी (Gaurav ji). It even works alone – a plain जी is a polite 'yes?'.

target: पहले डॉक्टर से बात कर लो।
english: Talk to the doctor first.
tip: You talk 'from' a person: डॉक्टर से (doctor se) = with the doctor. से stretches across English 'with', 'from', and 'by' – the verb decides which.

target: मेरे मौसेरे भाई-बहन हमारे बहुत क़रीबी रिश्तेदार हैं।
english: My maternal cousins are our very close relatives.
tip: Hindi has no single word for cousin – cousins are siblings with a tag: मौसेरे भाई-बहन (mausere bhai-behen) = brothers and sisters via your mother's sister.

target: मेरे दादाजी और नानाजी एक ही गाँव के थे।
english: My paternal and maternal grandfathers were from the same village.
tip: Grandfathers split by side: दादाजी (dadaji) is your father's father, नानाजी (nanaji) your mother's father. One English word, two Hindi people.

target: सत्तर प्रतिशत छात्र पास हुए।
english: Seventy percent of the students passed.
tip: पास here is the English loan 'pass': पास हुए (paas hue = became pass) means passed. It sounds like के पास (ke paas = near/have) – context separates them.

target: मेरी उम्र तीस साल है।
english: My age is thirty years.
tip: English says 'I am thirty' – Hindi states age as something you have: मेरी उम्र तीस साल है (meri umra tees saal hai = my age is thirty years).

target: अभी साढ़े तीन बज रहे हैं।
english: It is three-thirty right now.
tip: साढ़े (saadhe) before an hour adds a half: साढ़े तीन (saadhe teen) = 3:30. Only 1:30 and 2:30 use special words instead: डेढ़ (dedh) and ढाई (dhaai).

target: यह किताब मेज़ पर रखी है।
english: This book is kept on the table.
tip: Where English says the book 'is' on the table, Hindi says its state: रखी है (rakhi hai = is placed/kept). Things sit, lie or are kept – not just 'are'.

target: बारह महीने का एक साल होता है।
english: Twelve months make one year.
tip: होता है (hota hai) marks a general truth: बारह महीने का एक साल होता है (baarah maheene ka ek saal hota hai). Plain है (hai) = right now; होता है = always the case.

target: ढाई बजे तक सब काम ख़त्म कर लो।
english: Finish all work by two-thirty.
tip: Masculine -ा words shift to -े before a position word: बजा (baja) becomes बजे (baje) before तक (tak = by) – ढाई बजे तक (dhaai baje tak = by two-thirty).

target: आज तारीख़ बीस मार्च है।
english: Today's date is the twentieth of March.
tip: Dates commonly use plain numbers: तारीख़ बीस मार्च है (taareekh bees march hai = the date is twenty March). Hindi says 'twenty March' – no 'of' before the month.

target: दुकान सुबह नौ बजे खुलती है।
english: The shop opens at nine in the morning.
tip: No word for 'at' with times: नौ बजे खुलती है (nau baje khulti hai = opens at nine). The bare time expression carries 'at' by itself.

target: सवा चार बजे मीटिंग शुरू होगी।
english: The meeting will start at four fifteen.
tip: सवा (sava) before an hour adds a quarter: सवा चार बजे (sava chaar baje) = 4:15. A single word for 'quarter past'.

target: मेरे पिताजी एक सफल व्यापारी हैं।
english: My father is a successful businessman.
tip: Respect makes one person grammatically plural: पिताजी (pitaji = father) takes plural हैं (hain = are), not है. Elders and respected people usually get plural agreement.
